newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China Airlines to issue T$3.5 bln bonds.
newsitem.headline: China Airlines to issue T$3.5 bln bonds.

text.p: Taiwan carrier China Airlines said on Wednesday it would issue T$3.5 billion in seven-year domestic convertible bonds by the end of 1996 to raise funds to buy aircraft.
"These unsecured T$3.5 billion convertibles will be used to help finance our purchase of Boeing 747-400 planes," airline spokesman Liu Kuo-chien told Reuters.
The convertibles will be of two types.
The first at T$1 billion will bear a coupon rate of 5.0 percent with a yield-to-put option at a rate of 5.0 percent in the fourth or fifth year after issuance, Liu said.
The second, at T$2.5 billion, will bear a zero percent coupon rate with a yield-to-put option in the fourth year at 6.5 percent and a yield-to-put option in the fifth at 8.4 percent.
The conversion price is 101 percent of the average share price 10 days, 30 days and 60 days before conversion, he said.
The company has chosen Chinatrust Commercial Bank as the issue's lead underwriter, he said.
The issue is China Airlines' first of convertible bonds.
In May, the airline signed contracts to buy eight Boeing 747-400s at a total cost of US$1.4 billion.
Delivery of the first four aircraft is expected between May and December 1997, with options to buy the other four between 1998 and 2002, the company said.
